traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are implemented and verified: - Core functionality: `valid-annotation-format` supports configurable patterns via nested `story.pattern`/`req.pattern` and flat shorthand `storyPathPattern`/`requirementIdPattern`, plus corresponding example fields. - Backward compatibility: When options are omitted or invalid, the rule falls back to its original hardcoded patterns and examples, preserving prior behavior while reporting configuration errors where appropriate. - Pattern validation: Custom patterns are compiled as regular expressions; invalid patterns generate stable configuration error messages via `invalidRuleConfiguration` and do not break validation. - Error messages: Optional example strings feed directly into error messages for both story paths and requirement IDs; tests confirm custom and nested-over-flat precedence. - Quality and schema: Options are defined and validated using a JSON Schema attached to the rule’s meta, with `additionalProperties: false` and documented nested/flat forms in user docs. - Integration consistency: Default patterns and examples align with the `valid-story-reference` rule’s default directories and extension requirements, so the two rules can be used together without conflict. - Tests and documentation: Dedicated tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts cover all the REQ-* items for this story and pass, and user-docs/api-reference.md provides clear, user-facing configuration guidance. Given the concrete implementation and passing targeted tests, this story is fully satisfied.
